genderPolicy: Each role uses identical copy for its male and female artwork variants. These are fictional representative contributors, not newly identified historical people.
editionNote: Numbered examples are display examples requested by the user, not evidence that copies have been issued.

parent.title: Alexander the Great
parent.subtitle: King of Macedon
parent.bodyText: King of Macedon from 336 to 323 BCE, Alexander overthrew the Persian Empire and led his army into India. His conquests reshaped the ancient world and opened the Hellenistic age.

sources.title: The Rise of Macedon and the Conquests of Alexander the Great — Metropolitan Museum of Art

common.title: Campaign Soldier
common.subtitle: In the King's Ranks
common.bodyText: A campaign soldier drills with spear and shield, keeps equipment ready, and holds position beside the rest of the unit. Dependable service under orders lays the foundation for the judgment and responsibility of command.
common.sceneBrief: An adult Macedonian campaign soldier practising formation with spear and shield beside fellow soldiers; practical equipment, no messenger dispatch or stores duties.

uncommon.title: Campaign Squad Leader
uncommon.subtitle: Steadying a Small Command
uncommon.bodyText: A campaign squad leader directs a small group of soldiers on the march and in the field. Clear instructions, shared discipline, and care for the unit turn individual service into the first responsibility of command.
uncommon.sceneBrief: An adult small-unit leader gives clear directions to a few equipped Macedonian campaign soldiers; a modest field command, not a granary or provisioner scene.

rare.title: Campaign Staff Officer
rare.subtitle: Right Hand of the Great
rare.bodyText: A staff officer turns reports, routes, and supply figures into decisions the army can trust. Close to the command tent, careful judgment keeps scattered forces aligned with Alexander's astonishing ambition.

epic.title: Trusted Campaign Commander
epic.subtitle: The King's Proven Companion
epic.bodyText: A trusted commander bears responsibility for troops when orders become dust, noise, and danger. Courage joined to judgment makes the king's design hold together, earning loyalty that survives the hardest march.

parent.title: Aristotle
parent.subtitle: Philosopher of the Lyceum
parent.bodyText: Aristotle made inquiry a life's work, examining logic, ethics, politics, and the living world. At the Lyceum in Athens, his investigations helped establish enduring ways to observe, classify, and reason.

sources.title: Aristotle — Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
Aristotle's Biology — Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy

common.title: Lyceum Student
common.subtitle: First Questions of the Lyceum
common.bodyText: A Lyceum student records questions, studies arguments, and checks simple observations with the school. Careful notes and a willingness to test an explanation begin the habits that later support independent research and teaching.
common.sceneBrief: An adult student records questions and simple observations while learning in the Lyceum; introductory inquiry rather than general courier work.

uncommon.title: Lyceum Copyist
uncommon.subtitle: Scribe of Aristotle's School
uncommon.bodyText: A copyist preserves arguments with a steady hand, protecting distinctions that careless writing could erase. The work carries a lesson beyond the speaker's voice, giving the Lyceum's inquiry a lasting memory.

rare.title: Lyceum Researcher
rare.subtitle: Student of Aristotle
rare.bodyText: A researcher gathers observations and compares the accounts of others, bringing particulars before the school. Patient investigation strengthens the argument, ensuring that confident words remain answerable to the world they describe.

epic.title: Peripatetic Scholar
epic.subtitle: A Voice of the Lyceum
epic.bodyText: A Peripatetic scholar joins observation to disciplined argument and guides others through difficult questions. Independent judgment keeps the school alive, carrying Aristotle's spirit of inquiry into minds capable of challenging it.

parent.title: Euclid
parent.subtitle: Geometer of Alexandria
parent.bodyText: Euclid's Elements organized geometry and number into a powerful sequence of definitions, propositions, and proofs. Associated with Alexandria, this elusive mathematician gave generations a model of knowledge built through reason.

sources.title: Euclid — MacTutor, University of St Andrews
Who was Euclid? — Princeton University Press

common.title: Geometry Apprentice
common.subtitle: Learner of the First Principles
common.bodyText: A geometry apprentice learns to draw a circle and name what a figure contains. Small acts of precision begin a greater discipline, turning a curious eye toward the certainty of proof.
common.sceneBrief: A young adult apprentice draws one simple circle with dividers on a wax tablet or sand board, plain linen, modest courtyard.

uncommon.title: Geometrical Copyist
uncommon.subtitle: Scribe of the Elements
uncommon.bodyText: A geometrical copyist preserves diagrams alongside their arguments, keeping each letter faithful to its place. Exact work lets another reader follow the same path, protecting a proof from the smallest careless mark.

rare.title: Proof Checker
rare.subtitle: Keeper of Euclid's Reasoning
rare.bodyText: A proof checker questions every inference and tests whether a construction truly follows. This exacting reader guards the chain of reasoning, making an elegant conclusion worthy of the certainty it claims.

sceneBriefByGender.male: A proof checker works with a compass and ruler on a geometrical proof sheet. The head inclines gently forward in a natural three-quarter view and the eyes follow the compass tip on the sheet. Keep the neck relaxed above the shoulders and preserve the drafting hands, compass, ruler and nearby collaborator.

epic.title: Geometer of the Teaching Circle
epic.subtitle: Heir to the Elements
epic.bodyText: A teaching geometer leads others from a simple construction to an unexpected truth. Mastery turns difficult reasoning into a path others can follow, extending Euclid's enduring architecture one clear proof at a time.

parent.title: Lysippos
parent.subtitle: Master Sculptor of Sikyon
parent.bodyText: A celebrated sculptor from Sikyon, Lysippos worked chiefly in bronze and portrayed Alexander the Great. His lost originals survive through ancient testimony and later copies, preserving the influence of an extraordinary workshop.

sources.title: Lysippos — Getty Union List of Artist Names
Power and Pathos: exhibition checklist — J. Paul Getty Museum

common.title: Workshop Apprentice
common.subtitle: At the Sculptor's Bench
common.bodyText: A workshop apprentice prepares clay, tends tools, and watches experienced hands shape a figure. Familiarity with the material slowly becomes judgment, laying the humble foundation from which convincing bronze can rise.
common.sceneBrief: A simply dressed workshop apprentice prepares clay or wax at a low bench, bronze casting workshop behind, no master portrait pose.

uncommon.title: Bronze Workshop Assistant
uncommon.subtitle: Hand of the Lysippan Workshop
uncommon.bodyText: A bronze workshop assistant prepares moulds and materials with care the finished statue will never reveal. Reliable craft protects the sculptor's intention, helping fragile beginnings survive the demanding passage into metal.

rare.title: Portrait Modeller
rare.subtitle: Student of Lysippos
rare.bodyText: A portrait modeller studies the turn of a head and the balance of a stance. Sensitive hands give character to the clay, finding the living presence that a successful casting must preserve.

epic.title: Master of Lysippan Form
epic.subtitle: Bearer of the Master's Craft
epic.bodyText: A master sculptor unites proportion, gesture, and command of bronze into a figure that seems alive. Such judgment carries the workshop's tradition forward, making technical mastery serve an unmistakable human presence.

parent.title: Pytheas of Massalia
parent.subtitle: Explorer of the Northern Seas
parent.bodyText: An explorer from Massalia, Pytheas described Britain and the distant north in a work now lost. Later writers preserve fragments of his observations, leaving a remarkable voyage whose route remains debated.

sources.title: Pytheas — Oxford Dictionary of National Biography
Pytheas of Massalia — Encyclopedia of Ancient History

common.title: Deckhand of Massalia
common.subtitle: Crew of the Northern Venture
common.bodyText: A deckhand handles rope, cargo, and the small repairs that keep a vessel ready. Steady labour gives the expedition its footing, making the next unfamiliar coast possible long before it appears.
common.sceneBrief: A common deckhand coils hemp rope aboard a simple Massaliot merchant vessel; coarse tunic, harbour or calm sea, no elite equipment.

uncommon.title: Navigation Assistant
uncommon.subtitle: Learning the Northern Route
uncommon.bodyText: A navigation assistant checks bearings, compares coastal landmarks, and records the observations needed to keep an expedition on course. Practical work beside experienced navigators prepares the eye and judgment for independent observation.
uncommon.sceneBrief: An adult navigation assistant works on bearings, coastal landmarks or a voyage record aboard an ancient expedition vessel; no provision-loading task.

rare.title: Navigation Observer
rare.subtitle: Eyes of the Northern Voyage
rare.bodyText: A navigation observer records winds, daylight, and the changing outline of the shore. Attentive comparison turns passing impressions into useful knowledge, helping the expedition find order beyond the waters it already knows.

epic.title: Keeper of the Northern Voyage Log
epic.subtitle: Witness to Pytheas' Horizon
epic.bodyText: The keeper of the voyage log joins scattered observations into an account others can examine. Disciplined memory carries the expedition beyond its own lifetime, preserving the difficult boundary between witnessed fact and wonder.

parent.title: Menander
parent.subtitle: Master of New Comedy
parent.bodyText: Menander made Athenian New Comedy a theatre of recognisable lives, misunderstandings, and uneasy relationships. His plays shaped later comic drama, giving ordinary human motives a place beside the grand stories of heroes.

sources.title: Menander — Oxford Classical Dictionary
Menander: author, transmission, and text — Dickinson College Commentaries

common.title: Rehearsal Assistant
common.subtitle: Learning the Comic Stage
common.bodyText: A rehearsal assistant follows scene copies, records cues, and helps the company try a comic exchange in performance. Attention to dialogue and timing gives early practice in the dramatic work that will grow into writing and staging.
common.sceneBrief: An adult rehearsal assistant follows a scene copy and records performance cues beside a New Comedy company.

uncommon.title: Stage Copyist
uncommon.subtitle: Scribe of Menander's Stage
uncommon.bodyText: A stage copyist keeps dialogue and cues in dependable order as the company rehearses. Careful words protect the rhythm of an exchange, allowing comic misunderstanding to land exactly where the playwright intended.

rare.title: New Comedy Collaborator
rare.subtitle: Partner in Menander's Craft
rare.bodyText: A dramatic collaborator tests dialogue against performance and shapes the movement of a scene. A sharp ear and generous judgment help the company turn a clever script into recognisable, breathing human comedy.

epic.title: Dramatist of New Comedy
epic.subtitle: Heir to the Comic Stage
epic.bodyText: A dramatist of New Comedy finds the hidden stakes in ordinary households and troubled affection. Command of character gives laughter its depth, carrying the tradition onward through stories audiences recognise as their own.

parent.title: Demetrius the Besieger
parent.subtitle: King of Siegecraft
parent.bodyText: Demetrius Poliorcetes pursued kingship through bold campaigns and spectacular siege machinery. His famous assault on Rhodes ended in negotiation, yet its scale fixed his enduring reputation as the Besieger of Cities.

sources.title: Demetrius I of Macedonia, Poliorcetes — Oxford Classical Dictionary
The Great Siege of Rhodes — Oxford University Press

common.title: Siege Labourer
common.subtitle: Hand of the Siege Train
common.bodyText: A siege labourer moves timber, rope, and stone where the builders need them. Endurance turns the engineer's design into solid material, raising the patient groundwork beneath a machine meant to challenge walls.
common.sceneBrief: A plain-clothed siege labourer carries timber or coils of heavy rope at a construction yard, unfinished timber tower behind; no advanced engineering instruments.

uncommon.title: Siege Workshop Assistant
uncommon.subtitle: Artisan of the Besieger
uncommon.bodyText: A workshop assistant shapes fittings and checks the ropes that larger engines depend upon. Exact preparation keeps immense forces under control, making the smallest sound component a quiet ally against the strongest wall.

rare.title: Siege Engineer
rare.subtitle: Mind of the Siege Train
rare.bodyText: A siege engineer brings measurement and mechanical judgment to a battlefield problem. By balancing reach, weight, and stability, the engineer turns raw power into a deliberate answer to the enemy's defences.

sceneBriefByGender.female: A siege engineer tests and measures a timber windlass. The head bows gently forward in a natural three-quarter view and the eyes follow the measuring rule and its contact point on the mechanism. Keep the neck relaxed above the shoulders and preserve both hands, rule, rope and timber mechanism.

epic.title: Director of Siege Works
epic.subtitle: Right Hand of the Besieger
epic.bodyText: The director of siege works commands workshops, materials, and crews as parts of one great undertaking. Decisive coordination makes formidable machines possible, giving Demetrius' ambition a structure strong enough to bear its own weight.

parent.title: Theophrastus
parent.subtitle: Scholar of the Living World
parent.bodyText: Aristotle's colleague and successor at the Lyceum, Theophrastus explored philosophy and the natural world. His surviving botanical treatises gathered and compared plant knowledge, establishing a foundation for the systematic study of plants.

sources.title: Theophrastus — Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy

common.title: Garden Attendant
common.subtitle: Tending the Scholar's Garden
common.bodyText: A garden attendant waters specimens and notices the small changes of another growing day. Patient care keeps living examples within reach, giving the school's larger questions roots in plants that can be observed.
common.sceneBrief: A modest garden attendant waters or tends several plant specimens in a Greek courtyard garden; simple tunic, no master scholar's collection of instruments.

uncommon.title: Plant Records Assistant
uncommon.subtitle: Scribe of Theophrastus' Garden
uncommon.bodyText: A plant records assistant notes where a specimen grows and how it changes through the season. Careful description saves details that memory would blur, giving later comparisons a dependable place to begin.

rare.title: Comparative Plant Investigator
rare.subtitle: Student of Theophrastus
rare.bodyText: A plant investigator compares roots, leaves, habitats, and patterns of growth across living specimens. Discerning attention turns a garden of separate examples into evidence, helping the school recognise the order within abundance.

epic.title: Peripatetic Botanical Scholar
epic.subtitle: A Voice of Theophrastus' School
epic.bodyText: A botanical scholar brings many observations together and teaches others how to question them. Broad understanding gives the garden a lasting intellectual life, carrying Theophrastus' investigation beyond a single place or season.

parent.title: Zeno of Citium
parent.subtitle: Founder of the Stoa
parent.bodyText: Teaching at Athens' Painted Porch, Zeno founded the Stoic school around 300 BCE. His philosophy placed virtue and reason at the centre of a demanding vision of how a life should be lived.

sources.title: Stoicism — Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy

common.title: Listener at the Stoa
common.subtitle: First Steps Beside Zeno
common.bodyText: A listener beneath the porch gives a difficult argument the attention it deserves. Honest willingness to reconsider an easy answer marks the first small victory of reason over habit.
common.sceneBrief: A plainly dressed adult listener beside the painted colonnade holds a simple wax tablet, thoughtful attentive gaze; not posed as the school's teacher.

uncommon.title: Student of the Stoa
uncommon.subtitle: Pupil of Zeno
uncommon.bodyText: A student of the Stoa tests inherited opinions against reason and daily conduct. Perseverance gives the lesson substance, beginning the difficult work of making thoughtful judgment stronger than passing fear or appetite.

rare.title: Stoic Discussion Leader
rare.subtitle: A Steady Voice Beside Zeno
rare.bodyText: A discussion leader brings clarity and patience to the questions gathered beneath the porch. Careful challenge helps others examine their judgments, making philosophy a shared discipline rather than an impressive turn of speech.

epic.title: Scholar of Stoic Ethics
epic.subtitle: Bearer of the Stoa's Teaching
epic.bodyText: A scholar of Stoic ethics connects rigorous argument with the demands of a human life. Authority grows through consistency, giving the school a persuasive witness that reason can guide action when fortune turns.

parent.title: Ptolemy I Soter
parent.subtitle: Founder of a Dynasty
parent.bodyText: A general of Alexander, Ptolemy secured Egypt after the conqueror's death and later ruled as king. His dynasty made Alexandria a royal capital and endured until the age of Cleopatra.

sources.title: Ptolemy I Soter — Digital Egypt, University College London

common.title: Junior Court Official
common.subtitle: First Duties in Ptolemy's Service
common.bodyText: A junior court official checks names on petitions, copies routine entries, and prepares papers for review by experienced clerks. Careful work under supervision begins the administrative judgment that later supports accounts, supply, and government.
common.sceneBrief: A clearly adult junior official sits at a modest wooden desk in an early Ptolemaic administrative office, checking a short petition against a wax tablet with a stylus. The official's gaze follows the working task, shoulders and hands connect naturally, and the clothing is practical linen with a restrained ochre mantle. Small local duties under supervision; no courier movement, dispatch scroll held against the body, royal regalia, treasury or authority over a large office.

uncommon.title: Egyptian Administration Clerk
uncommon.subtitle: Scribe of Ptolemy's Court
uncommon.bodyText: An administration clerk keeps petitions, accounts, and orders in a form officials can use. Exact records give authority a memory, allowing the machinery of government to answer practical needs beyond the palace walls.

rare.title: Ptolemaic Supply Commissioner
rare.subtitle: Keeper of Ptolemy's Lifelines
rare.bodyText: A supply commissioner coordinates stores and transport across competing demands. Judgment turns figures on a tablet into provisions where they are needed, giving Ptolemy's government the material strength to maintain its hold on Egypt.

sceneBriefByGender.male: A supply commissioner checks a grain consignment and its seal while comparing the shipment with a wooden writing tablet. Keep the chin gently lowered and the gaze directed toward the inspected seal and records, with a relaxed neck aligned naturally above the shoulders. Preserve the hands, tablet, grain sacks, scales and harbour.
sceneBriefByGender.female: A supply commissioner checks a grain consignment and its seal while comparing the shipment with a wooden writing tablet. Keep the chin gently lowered and the gaze directed toward the inspected seal and records, with a relaxed neck aligned naturally above the shoulders. Preserve the hands, tablet, grain sacks, scales and harbour.

epic.title: Steward of Egyptian Government
epic.subtitle: Trusted Adviser of Ptolemy
epic.bodyText: A senior steward draws revenue, supply, and official reports into a coherent view of the realm. Trusted judgment turns separate offices into lasting government, helping Ptolemy's authority endure beyond a single command or campaign.

parent.title: Cleomenes of Naucratis
parent.subtitle: Financier of Alexander's Egypt
parent.bodyText: Appointed by Alexander to administer Egyptian revenue, Cleomenes became a powerful financial official. His control of grain and taxation amassed wealth, while ancient accounts also preserve accusations of ruthless exploitation and profiteering.

sources.title: Cleomenes of Naucratis — Oxford Classical Dictionary
Money and Prices in the Papyri, Ptolemaic Period — Oxford University Press

common.title: Granary Tally Assistant
common.subtitle: Counting Egypt's Grain
common.bodyText: A granary tally assistant counts grain measures, compares receipts, and records stores entering or leaving the granary. A checked tally begins the accounting discipline needed to manage revenue and the supply of a province.
common.sceneBrief: An adult granary tally assistant checks grain measures and receipts while recording stores entering or leaving the granary.

uncommon.title: Revenue Records Assistant
uncommon.subtitle: Scribe of the Nile Treasury
uncommon.bodyText: A revenue assistant checks receipts and records the passage of money and grain. Patient accuracy makes the treasury's figures traceable, giving its larger decisions a firmer basis than rumour, pressure, or convenient memory.

rare.title: Grain Supply Auditor
rare.subtitle: Examiner of the Granaries
rare.bodyText: A grain auditor compares the ledger with the storehouse and questions what fails to agree. Independent scrutiny gives administration its necessary resistance, exposing the costly distance between a promising account and an empty bin.

epic.title: Steward of Egyptian Grain Accounts
epic.subtitle: Keeper of the Harvest Reckoning
epic.bodyText: A senior grain steward reconciles reports from granaries, markets, and transport routes into one accountable picture. Command of the whole system makes this office a powerful guardian of Egypt's reserves and obligations.

parent.title: Nearchus
parent.subtitle: Admiral of Alexander's Fleet
parent.bodyText: Nearchus commanded Alexander's fleet from the Indus towards the Persian Gulf. His account of the difficult coastal voyage, preserved through later writers, joined practical seamanship to an enduring record of unfamiliar shores.

sources.title: Arrian, Indica — Fordham University Ancient History Sourcebook
Arrian on Nearchus' voyage home — Livius

common.title: Fleet Deckhand
common.subtitle: Crew of Nearchus' Ships
common.bodyText: A fleet deckhand tends lines, stows gear, and answers the work of another tide. Dependable hands keep the vessel ready for orders, giving the admiral's distant destination a practical beginning on deck.
common.sceneBrief: A humble fleet deckhand tends rigging on an ancient expedition ship, simple working tunic, salt-worn rope, coastal water behind.

uncommon.title: Coastal Scout
uncommon.subtitle: Eyes Along Nearchus' Shore
uncommon.bodyText: A coastal scout studies headlands, landing places, and signs of fresh water ahead of the ships. Alert observation gives the fleet its next safe pause, making unfamiliar coastline a place it can approach.
uncommon.sceneBrief: A coastal scout studies headland landmarks from a low ancient ship, holds a simple wax note tablet, practical tunic and cloak.

rare.title: Pilot of the Indus Fleet
rare.subtitle: Guide of Nearchus' Passage
rare.bodyText: A fleet pilot weighs currents, shoals, and the shape of the coast before setting a course. Seasoned judgment turns uncertain water into a passage others can follow, protecting the expedition when confidence alone would fail.
rare.sceneBrief: An experienced ancient fleet pilot compares a coastal sketch with the ship's bearing and distant shore, no magnetic compass or modern nautical tools.

epic.title: Navigator of Nearchus
epic.subtitle: Right Hand of the Admiral
epic.bodyText: A senior navigator joins pilots' reports, coastal knowledge, and the needs of the whole fleet. Responsibility reaches beyond one ship, helping Nearchus carry an exhausted expedition through the last demanding miles of its voyage.

parent.title: Eumenes of Cardia
parent.subtitle: Secretary and Strategist
parent.bodyText: Eumenes served Philip II and Alexander as a royal secretary before becoming a commander in the wars of the Successors. His career joined administrative skill to striking victories amid the struggle for Alexander's inheritance.

sources.title: Eumenes of Cardia — Oxford Classical Dictionary

common.title: Archive Attendant
common.subtitle: Keeper of the Ordered Shelves
common.bodyText: An archive attendant sorts bundles and returns each document to the place where it can be found. Quiet order gives the royal office a dependable memory, saving crucial words from the confusion of a crowded day.
common.sceneBrief: A humble archive attendant orders tied papyrus scroll bundles on wooden shelves in a Macedonian royal office, plain tunic and attentive expression.

uncommon.title: Royal Dispatch Copyist
uncommon.subtitle: Scribe in Eumenes' Service
uncommon.bodyText: A dispatch copyist preserves the wording of orders before they travel far from court. Exact attention keeps authority from changing with each retelling, giving officials a shared instruction they can read and answer.
uncommon.sceneBrief: A royal dispatch copyist uses a reed pen to copy a letter beside a sealed roll at a modest royal-office desk; no quill pen.

rare.title: Campaign Correspondent
rare.subtitle: Voice Across Eumenes' Lines
rare.bodyText: A campaign correspondent compares dispatches with the movement of forces and the needs of command. Clear writing draws scattered events into focus, allowing distant officers to act with a better understanding of one another.
rare.sceneBrief: A campaign correspondent compares a simple map and multiple dispatches at a field desk, practical cloak and reed pen, camp visible beyond.

sceneBriefByGender.male: A campaign correspondent compares a held dispatch with the map and writing surface under his pen. Keep a slight downward three-quarter head and a natural relaxed neck, with the eyes directed toward the dispatch and pen work. Preserve both hands, pen, papers, map, lamp and campaign tent.
sceneBriefByGender.female: A campaign correspondent compares a held dispatch with the map and writing surface under her pen. Keep a slight downward three-quarter head and a natural relaxed neck, with the eyes directed toward the dispatch and pen work. Preserve both hands, pen, papers, map, lamp and campaign tent.

epic.title: Secretary of Eumenes
epic.subtitle: Trusted Hand of the Strategist
epic.bodyText: A senior secretary turns reports and decisions into a record command can rely upon. Discretion, precision, and judgment give Eumenes a trusted hand, preserving the intent that holds an army's separate actions together.
